feedback.problem:
Let $V=C[1,e]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[1,e],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{1}^{e}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

If $x(t)={ln}^{2}⁡(t)+k$ and $y(t)=\frac{1}{t}$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{1}^{e}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}({ln}^{2}⁡(t)+k)\cdot \frac{1}{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡(t)}{t}+\frac{k}{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡(t)}{3}+k\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)){|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+k.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩ & =0 \\ \frac{1}{3}+k & =0 \\ k & =-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
